chunks: It is narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the excess in measure and weights, so he said: “If there has not been any transgression, then there is no harm.”

key_terms.الْكَيْلِ: measuring by volume in commercial dealings
key_terms.الْمَوَازِينِ: weights or instruments of weighing used in trade
key_terms.تَعَدًّى: transgression, unfair overstepping, or deliberate excess
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.فُضُولِ: excess or surplus beyond the base amount

ai.seo_question: Is incidental excess in measuring or weighing permissible in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning slight excess or discrepancy in measuring and weighing during transactions. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that when there is no transgression or unfair overstepping, there is no harm in it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3783 - It is narrated from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (as) about the excess that may result from measuring or weighing.
Imam (as) said: "If there is no deliberate excess (beyond fairness), then there is no harm."
